log.reply:
# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (stated as budget holder)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, 12 weeks, US$60,000
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. Its headquarters jurisdiction is the Netherlands, and it operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client reports three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work expected to start next year on a date that is not yet fixed.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three stated constraints shape the work:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Guided AI GRC Build is designed for this position. It closes the inventory gap early and puts governance around the deployed chatbot. It prepares a governed pathway for visual inspection to move from pilot to production. It also builds ISO/IEC 42001 readiness evidence ahead of formal certification work, without depending on that work having started.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement typically produces a governance system for the Client and then hands it over. A guided build reverses this. Your team builds the Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) in weekly workshops, refines it in coaching sessions and puts it to work through structured asynchronous assignments. At Week 12, the people who must operate the system are the people who designed it.

Three reasons favor this approach for Tamarack Instruments.

**Integration rather than duplication.** The Client lists an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system as incumbent frameworks. A guided build lets your team decide, week by week, how each AIMS artifact attaches to what already exists. This avoids a parallel structure. The Profile Block does not identify the specific registers, procedures or records within those systems. Each integration point is therefore recorded as `Unknown` below and will be confirmed with your team in Week 1.

**Retained capability.** The contracted outcome is a system your team can operate after the program ends. It is not a document set that depends on outside authors.

**Pace that matches the decision.** The program follows three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, visual inspection moves to production only when your team can show the governance around it. The calendar does not set that pace.

The program draws on three open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), the board-layer reference for steering checkpoints

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory sequencing for Weeks 2 to 5.** Systems enter the inventory in this order:

1. **The customer service chatbot first.** It is the only system stated as deployed. Its inclusion directly addresses the June 2026 audit finding.
2. **AI visual inspection second.** Its path to production in Q2 2027 is the Sponsor's stated objective.
3. **AI sales forecasting third**, recorded as a planned system.

Week 2 also includes a discovery exercise for any AI use not listed in the Profile Block. The existence of such use is currently `Unknown`.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The readiness themes below show how each week's artifacts can support future readiness. They do not represent or promise certification, audit or regulatory outcomes.

| Week | Spine focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Incumbent framework integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scoped to the three stated use cases. Roles assigned across the build team. Works council consultation pathway identified (confirm with external counsel). | Context of the organization; leadership | `Unknown` |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot entered first, visual inspection second, sales forecasting third. Discovery of unlisted AI use. | Context; planning | `Unknown` |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification approach applied to each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | Planning; risk criteria | `Unknown` |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot: GDPR and data residency considerations (confirm with external counsel). Visual inspection: quality and workforce impact considerations. | Planning; AI system impact assessment | `Unknown` |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Risks and treatments for the chatbot and visual inspection recorded | Planning; risk treatment | `Unknown` |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption. Policies with legal effect flagged (confirm with external counsel). | Leadership; policy | `Unknown` |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Pilot-to-production gate defined for visual inspection | Operation; lifecycle | `Unknown` |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review for inventoried systems (suppliers `Unknown`). EU data residency requirement applied to supplier terms (confirm with external counsel). | Support; operation; third-party relationships | `Unknown` |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Chatbot workflow governed with defined human oversight. Second workflow per the Week 1 decision. | Operation; human oversight | `Unknown` |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring defined for chatbot outputs and visual inspection performance | Performance evaluation | `Unknown` |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change procedures. First evidence review. | Operation; improvement | `Unknown` |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Walkthrough of at least four weeks of evidence. Readiness gaps recorded. | Performance evaluation; internal audit; management review | `Unknown` |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS comprising six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Dependency requiring a Week 1 decision.** Element 5 requires two governed AI workflows in production use by Week 12. The Profile Block states only one system as deployed: the customer service chatbot. Visual inspection is piloting, and its production target is Q2 2027. Whether it will be in production use by Week 12 depends on the start date, which is `Unknown`. It also depends on works council consultation, and the bearing of that consultation on visual inspection is `Unknown`. The second workflow is therefore `Unknown`. We ask that the Week 1 steering checkpoint confirm the second workflow, so that this element of the contracted outcome is achievable.

## 5. Client Team Commitment (Estimates)

The standing build team is drawn from the roles you named. The figures below are **estimates** of hours per person per week. They include the live workshop, coaching where relevant and asynchronous work, and will be refined at mobilization.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Heavier weeks (estimate) | Weeks expected to run heavier |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 hours | 5 to 6 hours | W1, W3, W6, W8, W12 |
| CISO | 3 to 4 hours | 5 to 6 hours | W4, W5, W8, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 3 to 5 hours | 6 to 7 hours | W5, W7, W10, W11 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 5 hours | 6 to 8 hours | W2, W4, W9, W10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 hours | 4 to 5 hours | W4, W7, W9, W10 |
| Internal auditors (two, each) | 2 to 3 hours | 4 to 5 hours | W8, W11, W12 |

**Internal auditor independence.** Two internal auditors are named on the build team. We recommend that the Client decide at Week 1 how their participation is structured, for example by focusing it on evidence design and readiness review, so that the independence of later internal audit work is preserved. The build lead from the Client side is `Unknown` and should be named at mobilization.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at three points:

- **Week 1:** mobilization brief covering scope, team, delivery risks and decisions needed, including the second governed workflow.
- **Week 6:** mid-point report covering spine status, the artifact register, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** closing report with an attestation against the six-element definition and an evidence sample index.

Steering membership is `Unknown` and will be confirmed with the Sponsor at mobilization. Checkpoint materials draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Participant locations and time zones are `Unknown`, so session times will be set at mobilization.

**Start date.** The start date is `Unknown`. As an illustration, a start in early January 2027 would place Week 12 before the start of Q2 2027.

**Price.** US$60,000. This sits within the stated approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year boundaries are `Unknown`, so please confirm that the program falls within the approved period. Payment terms and applicable taxes are `Unknown` and will be set out in the engagement agreement (confirm with external counsel).

**Data handling.** Program materials and any customer data references will be handled consistently with the Client's requirement that customer data stay in the EU (confirm with external counsel).

## 8. Next Step

Ahead of your decision date of 15 December 2026, we propose a 45-minute call to cover three items:

1. Confirm the start date.
2. Identify candidates for the second governed workflow.
3. Agree the engagement agreement for review (confirm with external counsel).

On signature, we will issue the Week 1 mobilization brief template and the build team onboarding pack.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
